name: Exercise Intolerance with Lactic Acidosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Exercise Intolerance with Lactic Acidosis Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Marked intolerance to physical exercise characterized by early fatigue and muscle weakness
Elevated blood lactate levels at rest and/or post-exercise demonstrating lactic acidosis
Muscle biopsy showing mitochondrial abnormalities or ragged-red fibers
Identification of pathogenic variants in mitochondrial or nuclear genes affecting oxidative phosphorylation
Abnormal results on exercise testing including decreased maximal oxygen uptake and early anaerobic threshold

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of exercise intolerance and elevated lactate levels plus either muscle biopsy abnormalities or supportive genetic/exercise testing findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires multidisciplinary evaluation including neurology, metabolic, and genetic assessments.

searchTerms: acid buildup in muscles at rest and after exercise
muscle acidosis during rest and activity

pathognomonic.symptomName: Rapid onset of muscle fatigue during exertion

common.symptomName: Muscle cramps during or after exercise

searchTerms: memory or focus issues after exercise

laboratory: Elevated blood lactate levels at rest and post-exercise
Increased creatine kinase in some cases
imaging: Muscle MRI showing selective muscle involvement and fatty infiltration
Cardiac MRI in cases with cardiomyopathy
genetic: Mutations in mitochondrial DNA genes (e.g., MT-TL1, MT-ND1)
Nuclear gene mutations affecting oxidative phosphorylation (e.g., POLG, TK2)
other: Muscle biopsy with ragged-red fibers and abnormal mitochondrial morphology
Abnormal exercise testing with early anaerobic threshold

distinguishingFeatures: Broader systemic involvement including neurological and cardiac symptoms
Exercise intolerance with muscle cramps and myoglobinuria
Severe lactic acidosis with neurological deterioration

redFlags: Severe lactic acidosis with metabolic acidosis
Development of cardiomyopathy or respiratory failure
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003;348(26):2656-2668.
Parikh S, Goldstein A, Karaa A, et al. Diagnosis and management of mitochondrial disease: a consensus statement from the Mitochondrial Medicine Society. Genet Med. 2015;17(9):689-701.
